text:
ales: FYI I'm hitting a flaky repro where streaming responses resume with interleaved bytes after an auth refresh. Seems different from the usual Last-Event-ID replay case.

ales: repro notes: client opens SSE, receives a large JSON event (10KB). During that event the client's short-lived token expires and the SDK refreshes auth, which triggers a reconnect. After reconnect the event fragments arrive twice and out-of-order: first the tail of the old event, then a mid-chunk piece, then the head. App sees corrupted JSON.

tom: can you paste the SDK code path? we recently changed auth refresh to do a background reconnect that reuses the same stream id.

ales: Node SDK flow:
```
// simplified
stream.on('data', handleChunk)
if (tokenExpired) {
  await auth.refresh()
  reconnectStream()
}
```
handleChunk does naive split on "\n\n" and JSON.parse each event.

ales: important detail: server annotates events with `id: sess-7:evt-<seq>` and sometimes splits long data lines across frames.

sophie: two likely culprits: (1) auth refresh triggers half-closed TCP leading to re-ordering at proxy layer; (2) SDK reconnect reuses connection flow and our client concat logic doesn't detect an abort boundary so it joins tail from old connection with head from new connection.

lucy: also note Go SDK treats comments (`:`) as invisible and strips them before split; Node kept them. That changes when a reconnect happens because some proxies emit keepalive comments on reconnect which can flip parsing behavior.

node-sdk: we've got `buffer += chunk` semantics. We try to be conservative but we flush when we see `\n\n`. If the server sends `data:` lines that include embedded `\n\n` inside JSON strings (escaped) we can also be fooled.

ales: exact failure trace I saw:
- seq 101: server sends bytes A (head)
- connection blip, client refreshes, reconnects
- server retransmits B (middle) and C (tail) but proxy merges frames as C,A,B on TCP reassembly
- client emits event with A+B merged incorrectly -> JSON.parse fails or produces garbage

tom: ops-bot, did we change any circuit-breaker or flow-control behavior in the proxy last week? Might be related.

ops-bot: we rolled a proxy patch that enabled more aggressive http2 stream window shrinking on 2026-03-15 03:14UTC (roll id pxy-1.9.4). It aimed to reduce memory spikes. Could affect mid-event fragmentation.

sophie: mitigation suggestions:
- SDK: never assume chunk boundaries correlate to event boundaries; always parse incrementally and validate JSON boundaries when `data:` content is JSON.
- SDK: on reconnect due to auth refresh, emit a synthetic boundary (e.g., drop any partial buffer) or tag buffered sequences with connection epoch so we don't merge across epochs.
- Server/proxy: preserve ordering per SSE `id` prefix and avoid retransmit reordering; or add monotonic `seq` header so client can reassemble.

lucy: parity note: Go SDK already tags frames with a connection-epoch id and will discard partial buffer on reconnect by default. Node SDK needs a similar flag: `discardOnReconnect=true` and an escape hatch `preserveTail` for apps that rely on lower-level merging.

ales: can we add an integration test to sample-app that exercises auth expiry mid-stream? E.g., short token TTL and a 30KB event. New hires keep tripping over this during onboarding.

node-sdk: sure, I'll add a mocha integration that runs against local proxy shim. Also adding metrics `sse.partial_drops` and `sse.auth_reconnects`.

tom: one more gotcha: some customers use Last-Event-ID dedupe but their ids are not unique across restarts (we reuse `sess-7`). Recommend we encourage `uuid:vN` style ids. We'll add a doc blurb.

ops-bot: creating an incident ticket INC-2026-314 for follow-up with proxy team. Priority P3 for now since limited customers affected.

ales: immediate dev tasks:
- node-sdk: add connection-epoch tagging + default discardOnReconnect=true, add integration test
- lucy: update docs + onboarding sample to force token-expiry test
- ops: evaluate rolling back aggressive window change if canary reproduces

lucy: I'll push a short README in the sample-app: `how to repro: set REDWOOD_TOKEN_TTL=3s && node long-event.js` and include expected behaviors.

ales: thanks. If anyone sees similar corrupted events in logs, please paste raw bytes (base64 ok) and the `id` headers.

node-sdk: filing PR shortly with tests. :rocket:
